scope: Ideal independent Bernoulli emission per pulse, declared threshold observation; not experimental validation or novel theorem.

threshold_countermodel.full_observed_laws: Equal iid Bernoulli law at original transmission for every sample size.

moment_countermodel.scope: Only first and second moments agree; full raw count laws do not.

matched_efficiency_benchmark.lower_bound_proof: For every transmission t in [0,1], p0=a*t, p1=eta*t-eta^2*t^2/4, difference=b*t*(1-t). Bernoulli KL <= chi-square <= b^2*t*(1-t)^2/[a*(1-a)] <= 4*b^2/[27*a*(1-a)]. Conditional KL chain rule applies to adaptive transmission policies. A decision with both errors <=alpha needs KL >= (1-2alpha)*log((1-alpha)/alpha).
matched_efficiency_benchmark.assumptions: Background-free; no deadtime, crosstalk, afterpulsing or fluorescence carryover; known simple hypotheses. Pair test has ideal zero false-positive probability. Hoeffding is a conservative sufficient budget, not a fair exact optimality comparison.
matched_efficiency_benchmark.conclusion: Any fixed-budget adaptive attenuation-only binary policy needs at least the stated lower bound; an ideal two-detector coincidence policy attains the stated upper bound. This is a rigorous shot-budget separation for these fixed alternatives, not an end-to-end cost or practical advantage claim.

dim_emitter_bound.statement: Adding emitters with total per-pulse detection probability at most epsilon changes the n-pulse full observed law in total variation by at most n*epsilon (coupling/union bound).
dim_emitter_bound.consequence: No uniformly finite reliable count certification over arbitrarily small positive brightness. Dark emitters give exactly equal full optical laws.
